title: Separate chamber visit dates permitted both signs of harebell timing contrasts in a 2021 North Wales data release
abstract: We tested how missing visit dates affect a timing summary in a North Wales ozone and warming experiment in 2021. We used 24 positive harebell count means from six chambers and four months. Exact bounds allowed each visit to occur anywhere in its stated month. Under one common date per month, two warming contrasts and one ozone by warming contrast were negative at all allowed dates. Under separate chamber dates, all five contrast bounds permitted both signs. The common-date 110 versus 30 ppb interaction bound was -4.075 to -0.136 days. Independent count errors with an upper factor of only 1.001713 were enough to let this bound include zero. This is an assumed error threshold, not a measured error. The method gives sharp schedule bounds for count-weighted snapshot dates. It does not identify true flower timing, a causal treatment effect or a climate trend. One chamber per treatment, one site and one year prevent independent regional or temporal tests. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and independent checks are included. External source records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Sharp date bounds for count-weighted snapshot contrasts. Blue uses one common date per month. Gray permits separate dates for each chamber. These bounds do not describe sampling uncertainty or true flower timing.
